[32931 Technology Research Methods | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

Understanding research methods and how they are used to validate the research is the focus of this subject. Gaining the necessary skills via a review of methodological strengths and limitations, understanding when and how techniques should be applied and how they should be presented are key for your degree. This subject aims to equip you with these skills will foster your professional skills by tailoring each to your research interests. To create a customised learning experience you will work in collaboration with a supportive team comprising of your subject coordinator and your supervisor. Together this supportive team, where you are at the centre, will engage in a self-directed journey to help you investigate how to close research gaps by using critical thinking, problem solving, effective communication abilities and most importantly research methods. This will be all in preparation for demonstrating research ability at this level

[32931 Technology Research Methods | Learning and teaching activities]
There will be an introductory session which will include information on developing a learning plan for research students. The session will also include exploration of learning opportunities and how they are suited to particular types of research aims.

 The remainder of the subject is an independent learning journey conducted in conjunction with your supervisor. You will define your goals, needs and strategies for meeting these. In some instances, your needs will be to enhance your existing research skills and in others, you will develop new skills. Together with your supervisor, you will identify what is appropriate to enhance your ability as you attend workshops and online courses. The increasing development of your skills will assist you in writing and refining your research as well as build on your ability to become a proficient researcher.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32931 Technology Research Methods | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Draw on the community of researchers to aid in the enhancement of ones own research abilities. (E.1)
SLO2: Reflect on implications of research knowledge, design and impacts on research to wider disciplinary community. (F.1)
SLO3: Present a rationale (Impact/significance) for the research study based on context, discipline, topic and population. (B.1)
SLO4: Customise research methods based on research objectives stated in research projects. (C.1)
SLO5: Justify disciplinary research methods to assure reliability and validity of research study. (D.1)
